nodes.summary: There is a sequence $G_0, G_1, G_2, \dots$ of pairwise distinct finite multigraphs, each with at least one edge, such that for all $i \ne j$ there is no cycle-continuous map from the edges of $G_i$ to the edges of $G_j$.
nodes.title: Samal's theorem: infinite antichains in the cycle-continuous order exist

nodes.summary: There is a sequence $G_0, G_1, G_2, \dots$ of pairwise distinct finite multigraphs, each with at least one edge, such that for all $i \ne j$ there is no cycle-continuous map from the edges of $G_i$ to the edges of $G_j$.
nodes.title: Infinite antichains in the cycle-continuous order

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a multigraph. A set $S$ of edges of $G$ is a binary cycle when $S$ is finite and every vertex $v$ is an endpoint of an even number of edges of $S$, where only edges with exactly one endpoint equal to $v$ are counted; loops are not counted, which agrees modulo $2$ with counting each loop twice. The cycle space of $G$ is the set of all binary cycles of $G$.
nodes.title: Binary cycle space

nodes.summary: A multigraph $G$ consists of a type $V$ of vertices, a type $E$ of edges, and a map assigning to each edge an ordered pair of vertices, its two endpoints. Distinct edges may have the same endpoints (parallel edges), and the two endpoints of an edge may coincide (a loop). Neither $V$ nor $E$ is required to be finite.
nodes.title: Multigraphs with loops and parallel edges

nodes.summary: Let $G$ and $H$ be multigraphs. A map $f$ from the edges of $G$ to the edges of $H$ is cycle-continuous when, for every binary cycle $C$ of $H$, the preimage $f^{-1}(C)$ is a binary cycle of $G$.
nodes.title: Cycle-continuous maps

nodes.summary: A multigraph $G$ is finite and nontrivial when its set of vertices and its set of edges are both finite and it has at least one edge. These are the graphs on which the cycle-continuous order is considered.
nodes.title: Finite multigraphs with at least one edge

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
